description:
StarNotes

A notebook and a drawable star map for your campaign, on an amber CRT screen.

Greetings, commander.

I'm bringing you a mod I've always wanted, a drawable in-game map and a simple notes editor, saved entirely in your in-game save. I've been playing this game for a good part of a decade, and while I do like the fleet log and creating map markers, I'd much prefer a map you can zoom in on and draw on, which is exactly what this mod is!

Returning to an old campaign after a while, it might be hard to remember what your goals were and where your stuff is, especially if you have more than one campaign. I don't want to fill up my actual notes app with video game notes that I won't look at either way, so I've included notes with checkboxes that you can cross out when they're done.

This UI mod works with the latest version of the game, but due to long campaigns and dev cycles, a version for the previous X patches will always be available if necessary.

I hope you enjoy the mod. Happy hunting, commander.

Mark where the good salvage was, circle the system you need to come back to, sketch a route along the slipstreams, and keep checklists for your colonies. Everything is saved inside your campaign.

The map: your own copy of the sector on an old amber monitor, with the game's grid, constellation and system names, live slipstreams (they follow the half-yearly reshuffle), the Abyss, and your fleet's position.
Drawing tools: pen with 5 colours, 3 thicknesses and solid, dashed or dash-dot lines. Also an eraser, markers (X, triangle, diamond, ring, target, sun, chest, skull), text labels, undo (Ctrl+Z) and clear.
Notes: as many note tabs as you like, each with a full text editor (selection, clipboard, word wrap). Turn lines into checklists and tick them off.

Press N on the campaign map, or open Intel > Exploration > StarNotes. The game pauses while it's open. With LunaLib installed you can rebind the key in its mod settings (F2).

Download and install

Install and enable LazyLib.
Download StarNotes.zip and unzip it into "Starsector/mods/". Or use the TriOS button above, which installs LazyLib too if you don't have it.
Enable StarNotes in the launcher and load a campaign.

Save compatibility: safe to add to an existing campaign. Not safe to remove from a campaign that was saved with it, so back up your saves first.
Version Checker and TriOS update checks are supported.

Changelog | Source on GitHub

Things you might ask
Q: Why not add drawing on the actual map?
The game doesn't support modifying its existing menus, and even if it did, it would be a bit too crowded, especially if the drawings showed up in other menus such as the Exploration tab. I want both maps to serve a purpose, one is for navigation and the other is for notes.

Q: Why no fuel range, starscape or exploration?
I don't want to replace the original map. The systems you've explored visibly glow more, so you can tell at a glance which ones you haven't visited. The screenshot shows it as well, the right side of the map isn't explored, for instance.

Q: Where are all the slipstreams?
It uses same data your normal map has, if you haven't found any you wont see any, but it you've already found some they will appear in the notes map as well when you install this mod.

Q: More tools for notes?
If theres any interest to complicate notes further. Theres already a mod for an older version that does exactly that called Fleet Journal https://fractalsoftworks.com/forum/index.php?topic=26122.0

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code: Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code)
Mod icon: made in the same Claude Code sessions
Graphics: none. The amber CRT look, map, toolbar icons and symbols are all drawn by the mod's own code at runtime, with no image assets.
Screenshots: taken in-game

I cannot write nor read code at all, however I've designed the mod, decided what it should do and how it should look and feel, and tested every change in my own campaign. Claude wrote the code to that brief and fixed what I found in play. The full source is on GitHub for anyone who wants to read it, because im definitely not going to.
